column1:
Cautiously positive tone: the FOMC highlights solid job gains, a strengthening labor market, and continued growth in household spending and business investment, but notes inflation (headline and core) running below the 2 percent objective with low market-based inflation compensation. In line with Friedman and Phelps’ natural-rate view, low unemployment cannot reliably buy sustained higher inflation, so the Committee’s emphasis on expectations and its symmetric 2 percent target is consistent with Woodford and Svensson’s frameworks where credible, state-contingent policy guides inflation expectations. The choice to keep policy accommodative and move “gradually” (including conditional balance-sheet normalization) aligns with Romer and Romer’s evidence on the costs of abrupt disinflation and lessons from the Volcker era about credibility. Net assessment: slightly positive overall, tempered by below-target inflation and subdued expectations.
